title: Mini-Project 1: Tip & Split Bill Calculator
overview: Build a real-world restaurant bill splitter that takes the total bill, a tip percentage (e.g. 15%, 18%, 20%), and the number of people sharing the table, then outputs the exact amount each person must pay.

steps.title: Gather User Inputs
steps.desc: Collect total bill amount (`float`), tip percentage (`float` or `int`), and number of people splitting (`int`).

steps.title: Calculate Tip and Total
steps.desc: Calculate tip amount (`bill * (tip_pct / 100)`) and add to the original bill to get the grand total.

steps.title: Split and Format
steps.desc: Divide the grand total by the number of diners. Format each person's share to 2 decimal places using `f"{share:.2f}"`.

checklist: Converts bill amount from string to float
Calculates tip percentage correctly
Divides grand total evenly among people
Formats final answer to 2 decimal places
starter_code:
# Tip & Split Bill Calculator
def calculate_split(bill: float, tip_percent: float, people: int) -> float:
    # 1. Calculate tip amount
    tip_amount = bill * (tip_percent / 100.0)
    # 2. Grand total
    total = bill + tip_amount
    # 3. Share per person
    share = total / people
    return round(share, 2)

# Test your function
bill = 100.0
tip = 15.0
people = 4
share = calculate_split(bill, tip, people)
print(f"Each person pays: ${share:.2f}")

tests.name: Standard 15% Tip for 4 People
tests.code: assert calculate_split(100.0, 15.0, 4) == 28.75, 'Expected 28.75 for $100 bill, 15% tip, 4 people'

tests.name: Zero Tip for 2 People
tests.code: assert calculate_split(50.0, 0.0, 2) == 25.0, 'Expected 25.0 for $50 bill, 0% tip, 2 people'

tests.name: 20% Tip for 5 People
tests.code: assert calculate_split(125.0, 20.0, 5) == 30.0, 'Expected 30.0 for $125 bill, 20% tip, 5 people'

title: Mini-Project 2: Number Guessing Game
overview: Create a classic number guessing game engine! Test guesses against a target number and return directional clues ('Too High', 'Too Low', or 'Correct!') along with attempt counting.

steps.title: Define Feedback Rules
steps.desc: Compare the guess to the secret target number. If equal, return 'Correct!'. If guess is higher, return 'Too High'. If lower, return 'Too Low'.

steps.title: Score Attempts
steps.desc: Calculate a score or rating based on the number of attempts: 1-3 tries = 'Amazing', 4-6 tries = 'Good', 7+ tries = 'Keep practicing'.

checklist: Returns 'Too High' when guess exceeds secret
Returns 'Too Low' when guess is less than secret
Returns 'Correct!' when guess matches secret exactly
Rates player performance based on total attempts

tests.name: Rating for 2 Attempts
tests.code: assert get_rating(2) == 'Amazing', 'Expected Amazing rating for 2 attempts'

title: Mini-Project 3: CLI Contact Book
overview: Build an in-memory contact management system using dictionaries and lists. Support adding new contacts, searching by name (case-insensitive), updating phone numbers, and deleting entries.

steps.title: Add and Update
steps.desc: Store contacts keyed by normalized lowercase name or inside a contact list with name, phone, and email attributes.

steps.title: Search and Retrieve
steps.desc: Implement `find_contact(book, name)` returning the contact dict or None if not found.

steps.title: Delete Contact
steps.desc: Implement `delete_contact(book, name)` returning True if removed, False otherwise.

checklist: Stores contact name, phone, and email in dictionary
Searches contacts case-insensitively ('alice' finds 'Alice')
Safely updates existing contacts
Returns None when contact does not exist instead of raising KeyError

tests.name: Add and Find Contact
tests.code: b = {}; add_contact(b, 'Bob Dylan', '555-1234', 'bob@music.com'); c = find_contact(b, 'BOB DYLAN'); assert c is not None and c['phone'] == '555-1234', 'Contact not found case-insensitively'

tests.name: Find Nonexistent Contact
tests.code: b = {}; assert find_contact(b, 'Ghost') is None, 'Should return None for unknown contact'

tests.name: Delete Contact
tests.code: b = {}; add_contact(b, 'Eve', '555-9999', 'eve@sec.com'); assert delete_contact(b, 'eve') is True and delete_contact(b, 'eve') is False, 'Delete logic failed'

title: Mini-Project 4: File-Based Quiz System
overview: Implement an automated quiz parser and scoring engine. Read questions, validate answers against error-handling edge cases, compute accuracy percentages, and format a results summary report.

steps.title: Parse Question bank
steps.desc: Iterate through quiz questions containing text, options, and integer answer indices.

steps.title: Safely Parse Learner Response
steps.desc: Write `parse_user_choice(raw_input, min_val, max_val)` that catches ValueError and bounds errors.

steps.title: Grade and Score
steps.desc: Calculate total correct, final percentage, and pass status (>= 75%).

checklist: Safely parses user choice string to 1-based integer with try/except
Handles non-numeric string gracefully without crashing
Validates answers against key
Returns structured report with score and pass/fail boolean

tests.name: Parse Valid Choice
tests.code: assert parse_user_choice('2', 4) == 2, 'Valid input 2 should parse as 2'

tests.name: Handle Non-numeric String
tests.code: assert parse_user_choice('abc', 4) is None, 'Non-numeric input must return None'

tests.name: Handle Out of Range Choice
tests.code: assert parse_user_choice('5', 4) is None, 'Out-of-range option must return None'

tests.name: Grade Perfect Score
tests.code: res = grade_quiz([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]); assert res['passed'] is True and res['pct'] == 100.0, 'Expected 100% pass'

title: Mini-Project 5: Password Generator & Security Analyzer
overview: Create a password generator and strength evaluator. Build passwords with configurable length, numbers, and symbols, and evaluate strength score (1-5) based on length and character diversity using Python built-ins like any() and string constants.

steps.title: Analyze Password Strength
steps.desc: Check for: length >= 8, uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Assign 1 point per criterion.

steps.title: Generate Secure Password
steps.desc: Combine character pools and select random characters using `random.choice()` ensuring all required categories are present.

checklist: Uses string or character checks for uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols
Uses any() to evaluate presence of each character category
Calculates strength score between 0 and 5
Generates random passwords meeting target length

tests.name: Weak Password Test
tests.code: assert check_strength('abc') == 1, 'Short lowercase password should score 1'

tests.name: Strong Password Test
tests.code: assert check_strength('Secret123!') == 5, 'Length 8+ with upper, lower, digit, and punctuation should score 5'

tests.name: Generate Target Length
tests.code: p = generate_password(16); assert len(p) == 16, 'Generated password should have length 16'
